top_choice_rationale: Targeted protein degradation is a new mode of small-molecule action: a designed bifunctional molecule forms a ternary complex with a target and an E3 ligase so that the cell removes the target. Its design variables (ligase ligand, linker, cooperativity) are chemical and measurable, the principle is reproduced across many ligases and laboratories, and it has opened targets once called undruggable. Crews, Deshaies and Ciulli form a coherent trio under a heterobifunctional-degrader citation that leaves the cereblon glue strand to the background text. The lack of an approved degrader is a clinical milestone and does not weaken the established mechanism. Base editing by Liu alone is my second choice, and condensates come last among the awards because they are the least settled.
